resources.title: SQL Server DBA Architecture & Operations Infographic
resources.description: A four-panel visual reference covering the full DBA operating picture: how client apps, the SQL Server instance, databases, and storage fit together; the full/differential/transaction-log backup strategy and which recovery scenario each one solves; the identify-analyze-optimize-monitor performance tuning loop and where indexes, statistics, memory, I/O, and query tuning each fit; and a high-availability/disaster-recovery topology showing Always On failover alongside offsite backups to Azure.

resources.title: Oracle Database Architecture Infographic
resources.description: A full visual walkthrough of how an Oracle database actually processes a request: client apps through the listener into the instance's SGA (buffer cache, shared pool, redo log buffer) and background processes (DBWn, LGWR, CKPT, SMON, PMON), down to the database's data files, control files, and online redo logs. Includes the step-by-step parse-execute-read-commit-redo-to-disk flow, the CDB/PDB multitenant architecture, and how tablespaces relate to data files — a quick reference for mapping SQL Server concepts onto Oracle's terms.

resources.title: NoSQL Database Types & Document/Graph Model Infographic
resources.description: A four-panel reference mapping the NoSQL landscape: the four major NoSQL families (document, key-value, column-family, graph) and where each fits; MongoDB's document structure, sharded-cluster architecture, and config servers; a side-by-side of MongoDB, Amazon DocumentDB, and Azure Cosmos DB's document API on the same document model; and how graph databases (Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, Cosmos DB's Gremlin API) store nodes and relationships, with real example use cases for each.

resources.title: Azure Cosmos DB Architecture Overview Infographic
resources.description: A single-page breakdown of Cosmos DB's global architecture: the five API models (Core/SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table) mapped to the data model each one fits, the database-container-item-partition key-throughput hierarchy, the end-to-end request flow from client through the API gateway into a distributed region, and the four consistency levels (strong, bounded staleness, session, eventual) with the latency/consistency tradeoff each one makes.

resources.title: Microsoft Cosmos DB Overview Infographic
resources.description: A real-world-framed overview of Cosmos DB as a multi-model, globally distributed service: how the same account can serve a web app, mobile app, and analytics workload through its five APIs, how data replicates across regions for low-latency reads worldwide, and a concrete e-commerce example using the SQL API for product data, the MongoDB API for user profiles, and the Graph API for behavior analysis.
